audit archive.description:
Archive the store: write a pack to immutable storage, read it back, verify it, record it, prune through it.

The pack runs from the end of the last archive (or the store's start) to
the last anchor. Nothing is recorded or pruned unless every file was
written and read back matching the manifest the NA signed, and the pack
read back verifies (``audit verify``, with the NA's anchors and executor
keys; ``--force`` records it anyway). Needs a privileged key.

audit verify.description:
Verify an audit pack offline, from the root key and the anchors you hold.

No network, no private key. Every NA signature is checked against the
key valid at the record's own time, from the root key down; executor
keys only from registry records the NA signed (or --executor-keys).
Decisions are judged as of their own time. Exits 1 when a check fails
or a change from --changes has no record.

The entries a pack cites (cited.jsonl) are checked by their signatures;
give the packs you verified before (--prior) or anchors at their
positions to tie them to the store. Each one neither covers is a
warning (cited_entry_unanchored).

 
    genesis-mesh audit verify pack-2026 --anchor root.pub \
        --known-anchors /audit/anchors --changes cloud-log.csv

parameters.name: root_key
parameters.help: The root public key you hold (base64 or a key file): the pack's keys prove nothing alone.

parameters.name: anchors_path
parameters.help: Anchors you hold: a directory from 'evidence anchors fetch', or a JSON file. Without them the pack proves its integrity, not that nothing was removed (warning no_held_anchors).

parameters.name: prior_dirs
parameters.help: A pack verified before (repeatable): the entries this pack cites must equal the ones it holds.

parameters.name: period
parameters.help: Two RFC 3339 times: fail when the pack does not cover this period.

parameters.name: report_path
parameters.help: Write the report this verification renders (from what it verified) to this file.

parameters.name: executor_keys_path
parameters.help: Executor keys you hold, for a store without registry records.

parameters.name: changes_path
parameters.help: Changes from a log outside Genesis Mesh (CSV or JSON) to match against the pack.

parameters.name: tolerance_seconds
parameters.help: How far apart a change and its record may be when matched by time.

audit verify.execution: CLI reference only. Check the coverage resource for MCP equivalents.

evidence anchors fetch.description:
Copy the NA's anchors into a directory you control.

Every run reads all anchors the NA serves and compares each one with the
copy you hold: if the NA serves a different anchor at any position you
hold, or no longer serves one, nothing is written and the command fails.
The NA's anchor history was rewritten or removed, and your copy is the
evidence. Otherwise the whole set is checked (NA signature, unbroken
chain) and missing positions are written, one file each; existing files
are never replaced.

Run it on a schedule with --anchor-now from a machine and storage the
NA's operators cannot change: the schedule bounds how long a new record
can be removed without detection.

 
    genesis-mesh evidence anchors fetch --na https://na.example \
        --na-public-key na.pub --out /audit/anchors --anchor-now \
        --operator-key auditor.key --operator-key-id auditor

parameters.name: na_keys
parameters.help: The NA public key you trust: base64 or a key file. Repeatable (key succession).

parameters.name: out_dir
parameters.help: Directory that holds your copy of the anchors (created if missing).

parameters.name: sovereign_id
parameters.help: Refuse anchors from any other sovereign.

parameters.name: anchor_now
parameters.help: Ask the NA to anchor its current head first, so recent entries are covered.

parameters.name: operator_key
parameters.help: Operator private key (the read tier is enough).

evidence anchors fetch.execution: CLI reference only. Check the coverage resource for MCP equivalents.

evidence verify-export.description:
Verify an evidence export: envelopes, store chain, signatures and chains.

With --known-anchors, the export is also checked against anchors kept
outside the Network Authority: a record removed or rewritten before an
anchored position, or an export that stops before the newest anchor,
fails. The export must start at entry 1 or, after retention, contain the
retention checkpoint that removed the entries before it; --from-anchor
accepts an export that starts right after a held anchor instead.

Example:

 
    genesis-mesh evidence verify-export \
        --file export.jsonl --na-public-key <base64> \
        --executor-keys executor-keys.json --known-anchors anchors/

parameters.name: na_keys
parameters.help: NA public key: base64 or path to a public key file. Repeatable (each valid at every time).

parameters.name: key_history_path
parameters.help: The NA's key history (GET /na/key-history): each NA key valid at its own times (v1.5.0). Needs --root-key.

parameters.name: root_key
parameters.help: The root public key you hold (base64 or a key file), for --key-history.

parameters.name: anchors_path
parameters.help: Anchors you hold: a directory from 'evidence anchors fetch', or a JSON file (v1.2.0).

parameters.name: partial
parameters.help: The export is a deliberate slice: neither its start nor anchors after its last entry are checked against the anchors.

parameters.name: from_anchor
parameters.help: The export continues from a held anchor (an export since an anchored position): it may start right after that anchor's entry (v1.3.1).

trust agree accept.description:
Accept an Offer or Counter-offer, producing an AgreementRecord.

Two modes:

 
  Direct acceptance (responder, no counter):
    --offer offer.json --graph responder-graph.json --signing-key responder.key

  Counter acceptance (offerer accepts counter):
    --counter counter.json --offer offer.json --signing-key offerer.key

Counter acceptance produces a DUAL-signed record immediately.
Direct acceptance produces a half-signed record; the offerer must run
``trust agree cosign`` to finalize.

Example (counter flow):

 
    genesis-mesh trust agree accept \
        --counter counter.json --offer offer.json \
        --signing-key aspayr.key --key-id aspayr-2026 \
        --output agreement.json

parameters.name: offer_path
parameters.help: CapabilityOffer JSON. Required for direct acceptance or counter validation.

parameters.name: counter_path
parameters.help: CapabilityCounter JSON. When present, offerer accepts the counter.

parameters.name: graph_path
parameters.help: Responder's graph (required for direct acceptance only).

parameters.name: output
parameters.help: Output path for the AgreementRecord JSON.

trust agree accept.execution: CLI reference only. Check the coverage resource for MCP equivalents.

trust agree cosign.description:
Add a second party's signature to finalize a half-signed AgreementRecord.

Used after direct offer acceptance (``trust agree accept --offer``).
The offerer calls this to add their co-signature over the same canonical form.

Example:

 
    genesis-mesh trust agree cosign \
        --agreement half-agreement.json \
        --signing-key aspayr.key --key-id aspayr-2026 \
        --output agreement-final.json

parameters.name: output
parameters.help: Output path for the finalized dual-signed AgreementRecord JSON.

trust token issue.description:
Issue a signed Invocation-Bound Capability Token (IBCT).

The token carries an attenuated subset of capabilities from the source
agreement (or delegation), expires at --valid-for seconds, and optionally
limits the bearer to --max-invocations uses.

Example (simple, 5-minute token):

 
    genesis-mesh trust token issue \
        --agreement agreement.json \
        --bearer agent-b \
        --caps "transactions.read" \
        --signing-key operator.key --key-id op-2026 \
        --output token.json

Example (budget-limited + constraint):

 
    genesis-mesh trust token issue \
        --agreement agreement.json \
        --bearer agent-b \
        --caps "transactions.read,audit.read" \
        --max-invocations 5 \
        --constraint "not_before:2026-07-01T00:00:00Z" \
        --signing-key operator.key \
        --output token.json

parameters.name: agreement_path
parameters.help: AgreementRecord JSON that grants the capabilities.

parameters.name: bearer_sovereign_id
parameters.help: Sovereign ID that will use the token.

parameters.name: max_invocations
parameters.help: Budget cap: maximum number of allowed uses. Omit for unlimited.

parameters.name: constraints
parameters.help: Policy constraint string. Repeatable. Supported: not_before:ISO8601, peer_sovereign:sovereign_id

parameters.name: delegation_path
parameters.help: DelegatedAgreementRecord JSON when the token is derived from a delegation.

parameters.name: output
parameters.help: Output path for the signed InvocationToken JSON.

trust token record-use.description:
Record a single token invocation.

Links to the prior use-record when --prior is supplied, forming a
tamper-evident use chain.

Example (first use):

 
    genesis-mesh trust token record-use \
        --token token.json \
        --action "transactions.read" \
        --outcome success \
        --signing-key agent.key --key-id agent-2026 \
        --output use-1.json

Example (chained use):

 
    genesis-mesh trust token record-use \
        --token token.json \
        --action "transactions.read" \
        --outcome success \
        --prior use-1.json \
        --signing-key agent.key \
        --output use-2.json

parameters.name: action
parameters.help: Short label for the invoked action.

parameters.name: prior_path

trust verify-evidence.description:
Verify the signature on a TrustEvidence record.

Always checks the Ed25519 signature.  With --graph, also re-derives the
graph digest and confirms the evidence was produced over the same graph state.

Example:

 
    # Signature check only
    genesis-mesh trust verify-evidence \
        --evidence evidence-a-b.json \
        --public-key <base64-pub-key>

    # Strict: signature + graph binding
    genesis-mesh trust verify-evidence \
        --evidence evidence-a-b.json \
        --public-key <base64-pub-key> \
        --graph fleet-graph.json

parameters.name: evidence_path
parameters.help: Path to the signed TrustEvidence JSON.

parameters.name: public_key_input
parameters.help: Issuer public key: base64 string or path to a public key file.
